headline: The Indonesia long-form, now titled “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana”, has 44,132 views in 43 hours. Its subscribers reach the data in two or three days. The free slot goes to a follow-up long-form for its viewers. The Tipu Short is due tomorrow and nothing is scripted.

top3.topic: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: due tomorrow, nothing scripted
top3.signal: Owner's pick of 15 November; the radar's step this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “tipu sultan history”. His birth date is disputed and the Karnataka row is out of the news.
top3.recommendation: Decision 1: script and record today, publish 20 November before 18:00 IST, judge on 23 November. If it cannot ship by 22 November, drop it and give the time to Tegh Bahadur.

top3.signal: The top-ranked dated moment, five days out, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. What it rests on: the date. Mughal and persecution Shorts without a film behind them have landed at or below the usual over the last six months.
top3.recommendation: Decision 2: script by 21 November, record on 22, publish the evening of 23 November, judge on 26. Sentence one is Aurangzeb's order, the place and the date.

top3.signal: The radar asks this week whether the date carries a long-form; its next step is due 23 November.
top3.recommendation: Not a long-form: the Bali long-form has that slot. Decide on 23 November; if Tegh Bahadur has shipped, one Short on a single documented act against India. No proof either way on this channel: its one Churchill Short lost viewers in its first seconds to background about the INA.

more.topic: Tarabai jails her own king, 24 November 1750
more.signal: On the radar for the same day as Tegh Bahadur, from a lower-confidence date source. The channel's Tarabai Short against Aurangzeb is one of its four breakouts.
more.recommendation: Not on this date: Tegh Bahadur has 24 November and one Short a day is the limit. Keep it as a later Short, the sequel to that breakout (see ideas).

skipped.topic: Rani Lakshmibai and Indira Gandhi on X today
skipped.signal: Both birthdays are trending on X in India today.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. A freedom-fighter biography and a recent prime minister are the two kinds of Short that have done below the usual here, and posting on the day itself has failed before.

skipped.topic: The Great Famine of 1876 to 1878 on Wikipedia
skipped.recommendation: Skip a remake: you already made it, as the Madras famine Short on Temple's wage, published 18 October.

whats_working: “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana” runs at 1,024.8 views an hour; the Asia long-form has averaged 323.2 an hour over its life. Its like rate is 1.7% against 0.9% for the Asia one. It now carries the title that says what was done to Ravana, not the search-led one. Judge it on day three, 20 November, and on subscribers when they arrive.
Long-form still brings most of the subscribers that uploads bring: 70.9% of upload-attributed net subscribers over 28 days, on 37.7% of upload views. That is why the free slot goes to a long-form.

The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 12.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the shape for the Bali script's ending: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”
whats_wrong: Neither open Short has a script on disk. Tipu is due tomorrow and lapses on 23 November if it does not ship, and the Tegh Bahadur script was due on disk today. Probable cause: the Indonesia launch took the week. Test: none. If the week holds only one Short, make Tegh Bahadur, the higher-ranked date, and mark Tipu dropped so the list stays honest.

Film reach is still not turning into subscribers: “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” brings 0.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Asia long-form 2. Long-form's rate over the 365-day window has fallen out of its usual range to 8.3, and only 41.5% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so part of the fall is how views are counted since August. Probable cause: the film videos answer a scene or tour a map and name no culprit. Test: the Indonesia long-form names who rewrote the story; around 22 November compare its subscribers per 1,000 with the Asia long-form's.

Long-form views fell 38.1% and watch time 41.3% week over week to 2026-11-16, with a median average view of 29.8%. Probable cause: the Asia long-form's Home-feed run ending, not a new fault; the Indonesia launch is not in those days. Test: the week to 23 November, which has the launch in it.

actions.action: Reply to the Indonesian viewer who says corrections are needed under “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana”: say what the video got right and what it should have said. /replies drafts it.
actions.rationale: It is a correction from the country in the story, under a video that is climbing, so new viewers read it. That a reply helps is a guess, not a measured effect.

actions.action: If not done yet, put the Indonesia long-form on the end screen and in the pinned comment of “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”.
actions.rationale: The Asia long-form has 156,794 views, the largest long-form audience the channel has, and the same subject.

actions.action: Make the Indonesia long-form the channel page's featured video for visitors who have not subscribed, while it climbs.
actions.rationale: 854 subscribers over 28 days came from the channel page rather than any video. That the featured video moves them is a guess.

actions.action: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” has 0 views since 3 November, and the two Shorts published with it, “Itihasa vs Myth” (82) and “Is Caste Unique to India?” (255).
actions.rationale: A public Short gets at least a handful of views, so no views at all points to its visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.

actions.action: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.
actions.rationale: Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing, so the website is left out today.

growth.verdict: Needs 225 net subscribers a day. The channel does 42.96/day, so the target is a **5.2x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "4. scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1276 of the 2,828 subscribers that 21 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 23.2/day (649 of 1,117 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 21 long-form and 104 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.3 more long-form videos a year — 38.3 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 32 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 135, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 454 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 23.2/day (649 of 1,117 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 8 revision long-form videos, median 58 subscribers, against 32 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 23.2/day (649 of 1,117 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,276 subscribers on 72,902 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.

growth.note: Long-form is 17% of uploads and ~80% of subscribers, converting 11.7x better per view than Shorts (15.07 vs 1.29 subs/1k over 365 days). The RATE is channel-wide from channel_totals_daily with no uploads filter, because uploads are a minority of this channel's growth: over 28 days to 2026-09-27 uploads produced 117 net subs and the channel gained 830. Per-video figures come from own_video_lifetime (365d) and are upload-attributed by design, which is correct for judging videos and wrong for judging a target.
